long_biography.plain_text:
Morris grew up in a Liverpool shopkeeping family whose retail experience spanned three generations. At 21, he financed his own shop with a bank overdraft and opened it in the Old Swan district in 1976. The store, initially called Home and Bargain, focused on branded health, beauty and household products bought and sold at discount prices. Morris expanded the formula organically into the national Home Bargains chain.

The business remains privately and family owned. Morris is an active director and the person with significant control over its current holding company, with more than three quarters of the shares and voting rights. That control supports Retail as both his wealth-creation and current primary industry. Reported company valuations, sales, profits, properties and family-trust assets are not treated as his personal wealth.
